Alphabet.metaTitle: Thai alphabet: 44 consonants and 32 vowels with RTGS
Alphabet.metaDescription: The full Thai writing system in one table — all 44 consonants and the traditional 32 vowels, each with its Royal Thai General System (RTGS) romanisation and Thai name.
Alphabet.title: The Thai alphabet
Alphabet.intro: Thai has 44 consonants and 32 vowels. This is the whole system in one place, with the Roman spelling of each letter's name so you can say it before you can read it.
Alphabet.rtgsNote: The sound column uses RTGS, the Royal Institute's romanisation. It records neither tone nor vowel length, so สระอิ and สระอี are both written i — the name column keeps them apart.
Alphabet.consonantsBody: Each consonant is named after a word starting with it, the way English says "A for apple". Two sounds are given where they differ: the first is the letter at the start of a syllable, the second at the end.
Alphabet.vowelsBody: Vowels are written around the consonant, not after it — before, above, below or on both sides. Each short vowel is paired with its long partner.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.subtitle: The things people ask most often about learning English vocabulary and the Oxford 3000 word list.
Faq.a1: The Oxford 3000 is a list of the 3,000 most frequent and most useful English words, chosen by Oxford's dictionary team and grouped by CEFR level from A1 to B2. Knowing these words covers most of the English you meet in real use.
Faq.q2: How many English words should I learn per day?
Faq.a2: A lesson here is 8 words, about 2-3 minutes. Short daily practice beats long, occasional sessions, and the words you get wrong come back for review automatically.
Faq.q3: What is the difference between A1, A2, B1 and B2 vocabulary?
Faq.a3: A1 is the starting level: the most common basic words. A2 is elementary, for everyday life. B1 is intermediate, for study and work. B2 is upper-intermediate, for reading articles and preparing for exams. Work up from A1.
Faq.a4: Yes. Create an account to save your progress, the words you already know and the words you need to review — at no cost.
Faq.a5: You can read the words and their meanings without one. To have the app remember where you got to, which words you know and which need review, you need an account.
Faq.q6: How does the review system work?
Faq.a6: Every correct answer pushes that word's next review further out; a wrong answer pulls it closer. Words you got wrong are collected on the mistakes page so you can practise them straight away.

about.metaDescription: How this English vocabulary course is built for Thai learners.
about.intro: We help Thai speakers build durable English vocabulary through short, focused practice.
about.s1Body: The course is based on the Oxford 3000 and organised by CEFR level. Thai meanings and pronunciation support make each word approachable.
about.s2Body: Recognition, spelling and recall are mixed into short sessions. The server grades answers and spaced review brings words back when they are due.
about.s3Body: Seen, strong and mastered are different states. We show them honestly; opening a word does not mean it has been learned.

howItWorks.metaDescription: Learn how sessions, review and progress work in the vocabulary app.
howItWorks.intro: A clear path from a first five-word trial to daily recall and long-term review.
howItWorks.s1Body: Choose a CEFR level or try a public practice session. You can see value before creating an account.
howItWorks.s2Body: Each normal session has eight item slots and mixes meaning, word choice and spelling with lightweight warm-ups.
howItWorks.s3Body: Correct and incorrect attempts update a spaced-review schedule. Due words come before new material.
howItWorks.s4Body: A level is collected when its required words are strong. Mastery remains a longer-term stretch goal.

privacy.metaDescription: What learner data the vocabulary app stores and why.
privacy.intro: We collect the minimum information needed to run accounts, save learning progress and understand the acquisition funnel.
privacy.s1Body: Account email, username and authentication data are stored with progress rows in Cloudflare D1. Audio assets may be served from Cloudflare R2.
privacy.s2Body: First-party, secure cookies keep you signed in and preserve an anonymous practice claim. They are not answer keys and are not placed in URLs.
privacy.s3Body: Product analytics uses a separate pseudonymous identifier. We do not send the application user ID, email, typed answers, tokens or Thai meaning text to analytics.
privacy.s4Body: Signed-in learners can export their own portable progress. For correction or deletion requests, use the contact pathway available in the app; identity must be verified before account data is changed.

terms.metaDescription: Plain-language terms for using the vocabulary learning app.
terms.intro: Use the service for personal learning and treat its content and other users responsibly.
terms.s1Body: This is an independent learning tool, not an accredited school, examination provider or guarantee of a CEFR result.
terms.s2Body: Keep access credentials private and provide accurate account information. Do not attempt to access another learner's progress or administrative tools.
terms.s3Body: We work to keep the service reliable, but do not promise uninterrupted availability. Features and content may change as quality improves.
terms.s4Body: You may use the app for personal study. Automated extraction, abuse of practice endpoints and attempts to bypass access controls are not permitted.

contact.metaDescription: How to get help with the vocabulary learning app.
contact.intro: Start with the help available inside the app so your request reaches the right context without publishing personal information.
contact.s1Body: Use the in-app support pathway while signed in and describe the page and action that failed. Never include your password or a magic-link token.
contact.s2Body: Ask through the same verified account pathway for an export, correction or deletion. We may need to confirm account ownership before acting.
contact.s3Body: Report the English word, CEFR level and the Thai text that needs review. Corrections enter the content review queue rather than changing published learning data immediately.
